title: Create account

motion.why: The two screens are siblings; the form column swaps sides, so a fade-through reads as the card turning over rather than a slide

source.notes: Sign-up uses the same AuthShell layout as sign-in with the form on the right, a different photo (the apron at dusk) and highlights for new members. Fields come from the product: name, email, phone, password, account type (traveller, operator, hangar host) and terms.

audience: A first-time visitor who came from a listing, a charter quote or the home page, usually on a phone; they will give a name, email, phone and password if the form is short and tells them why each is needed.

sections.title: Create account
sections.purpose: The whole screen: brand, form and the media panel

highlights.title: Charter, buy or lease
highlights.text: Request a jet, make an offer on an aircraft or book hangar space from the same account.

highlights.title: Verified operators
highlights.text: Every operator and hangar host is checked for certificates and insurance before they list.

highlights.title: Pay when it is confirmed
highlights.text: Nothing is charged until the operator confirms your request.

elements.why: The reference product's split-screen sign-in, in Airiona: the form column beside a cinematic media panel (poster, looping video after load, scrim, grain, rotating highlight cards with progress ticks that pause on hover or focus); a slim photo strip on phones

alternatives.rejected: the old login: a mobile header stretched into an aside, no motion, no highlights, and the art fell below the form on phones
a multi-step carousel for first launch, not a sign-in screen

elements.notes: Sign-in puts the form left, sign-up right, so switching between them flips the card.

children.why: Help stays one tap away without competing with the form
children.notes: Opens the help centre in a new tab

children.text: Two minutes, then you can request flights, list an aircraft or book hangar space.

children.why: One name field: no first/last split, which fails for many names
Sign-in identifier and where confirmations go
Operators call to confirm departure details; the hint says so
New password with the rule stated before the user types, not after
Three always-visible roles in one tap; changes what the dashboard shows first

alternatives.rejected: hides three short options behind a tap

children.notes: The terms and privacy pages open from the footer links

submit.label: Create account
submit.action: POST /api/accounts { fullName, email, phone, password, accountType, terms }

success.title: Welcome to Airiona
success.text: We sent a confirmation link to your email. Open it to verify your account.

submit.failure: 409 (email exists): message under Email 'An account with this email exists. Sign in instead.'; 422: messages under the fields the server names; network: danger Toast with Retry and the form stays filled

inputs.hint: Operators use it to confirm departure details.

messages.phone: Enter a number with its country code, like +971 50 123 4567.

inputs.hint: At least 8 characters, with a letter and a number.

messages.pattern: Add at least one letter and one number.

messages.required: Choose how you will use Airiona.

fields.name: terms
fields.label: I accept the terms and privacy policy

messages.required: Accept the terms to create your account.

a11y: Password rules are in the hint before typing, and the pattern message names what is missing.
The account type group is labelled "I'm joining as"; arrow keys move between the three roles.
The terms checkbox error is announced (role="alert") and focus moves to it on submit when it is the first invalid field.
notes: No sticky bottom bar: the Create account button follows the last field and a sticky copy would cover the terms line (answers the lint warning about sticky.base bottom).
Sign-up shows the poster without video: the apron photo has no loop yet; add `video` when one is cut (export the poster from its first frame).
Operators and hangar hosts get a verification step after the first sign-in (certificates, insurance); it is not part of this form so the form stays short.
